summary: This bill amends federal criminal law to authorize the death penalty for aggravated sexual abuse, sexual abuse of a minor, and abusive sexual contact against children, and for rape of a child under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends criminal statutes to expand the availability of the death penalty for child sexual abuse offenses. It contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures of any kind.
The bill addresses only criminal penalties under title 18 and title 10 of the U.S. Code. It has no tax-related content.
No provisions in the bill concern healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
The legislation does not mention firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill is silent on immigration, border policy, or noncitizen offenses.
The bill concerns punishment for child sexual abuse and makes no reference to reproductive rights or abortion.
While the bill amends the Uniform Code of Military Justice to authorize the death penalty, the change is limited to sentencing options and does not alter defense spending levels or military budgets.
No environmental or regulatory provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No education policy, school funding, or curriculum provisions are present.
The legislation addresses sexual offenses against children, not controlled substances or drug enforcement.

The bill's core purpose is to expand the death penalty to additional categories of child sexual abuse under federal law and the UCMJ. This directly advances a policy of harsher criminal penalties and tougher sentencing for serious offenses, aligning strongly with the +1 end of the scale.
No trade, tariff, or international commerce provisions exist.
The bill contains no fiscal measures that would affect deficits or debt.
The legislation does not address sexual orientation, gender identity, or related civil rights.
No foreign assistance or international aid provisions are included.
The bill is unrelated to voting rights or election administration.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions appear.
The bill does not address employment law, unions, or worker protections.
No religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination language is present.
